body.statement: Let \(s,D,\tau,k\) be positive integers.  For a rational polynomial system with at most \(s\) predicates, degree at most \(D\), input-coefficient bit length at most \(\tau\), and one block of \(k\) quantified variables, a verified well-behaved one-block real-quantifier-elimination execution decides feasibility and computes a projection with one free variable using \((sD)^{O(k)}\) exact scalar arithmetic and sign operations.  Its projection and sign-cell sample-point encodings have algebraic degree \(D^{O(k)}\); every integer coefficient in the output or the attested well-behaved intermediate execution, and every rational isolating datum in the output, has bit length \(\tau(sD)^{O(k)}\).  Every nonempty sign cell admits an exact real-algebraic sample-point encoding within these degree and height bounds.

source.locator: Theorems 1.3.1 and 1.3.3, pp. 1003--1005, together with the well-behaved-algorithm and sample-point bounds in Sections 1.2 and 3
source.verbatim_statement: there exists an equivalent quantifier-free formula ... and the degrees of the polynomials P_ij(y) are bounded by d^{Π_i O(k_i)}
